items.text: Incorporated round 2 answered decisions into conclusion: (d1) Token TTL set to 24-hour default per user direction — agents will run longer as AI capabilities improve, so a generous TTL avoids mid-execution invalidation without requiring refresh. (d2) Single verify endpoint returning full claims — no separate introspection endpoint. (d3) Fail open with warning on verification failure — fall back to anonymous attribution, matching backward-compat model.

All 7 design decisions are now settled across rounds 1 and 2: token format (custom HMAC-SHA256), verification model (server-side), protocol (REST), claims structure (minimal + meta), TTL (24h default), endpoint contract (single verify), and failure handling (fail open). No open questions remain that block execution.

Remaining gaps documented in Limitations: (1) revocation store design (in-memory set vs DB column) deferred to implementation, (2) no load testing analysis, (3) HMAC secret rotation strategy unspecified, (4) fail-open may need revisiting for multi-tenant. These are implementation-time decisions, not research blockers.

Conclusion defines 3 concrete execute backlog items with dependencies: agent-manager-identity-tokens → cli-core-identity-consumer → swarm-manager-identity-adoption. Plus a future-work section for non-blocking follow-ups (secret rotation, audit logging, rate limiting).
